name: Lauraceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project Lauraceae through aromatic woody habit, simple exstipulate leaves, tiny trimerous flowers with valvate anthers, and a one-seeded fleshy fruit often seated in a cupule; then split Lindera from Camphora by deciduous/dioecious pseudoumbels versus evergreen triplinerved camphor-tree architecture.

project_scope.selection_mode: Lindera benzoin + Camphora officinarum project module
project_scope.note: Current Kew accepts both species. Lindera benzoin is native into Texas; Camphora officinarum is introduced in Texas and remains a nonlocal comparison rather than a native anchor.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the leaves and flower size. Lauraceae are usually aromatic woody plants with simple entire leaves and no stipules; the flowers are tiny, usually 3-merous, and the anthers open by little upward-lifting valves rather than longitudinal slits.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Trees or shrubs in the project pool. Leaves simple, entire, usually alternate, exstipulate, often aromatic and sometimes 3-veined from near the base.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers small, actinomorphic, usually with 6 tepals in 2 whorls of 3. Fertile stamens are typically in 3 whorls; inner stamens often have paired basal glands. Anthers are 2- or 4-locular and open by flap-like valves. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with one ovule.
family_diagnostics.fruit: One-seeded berry or drupe, often seated in or partly surrounded by an enlarged floral receptacle/cupule.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Aromatic woody plant + no stipules + tiny 3-merous flowers + valvate anthers + one-seeded fleshy fruit is the durable family door.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: leaf/stipule check → tiny 3-merous flower → valvate anther → one-seeded fruit/cupule → Lindera door → Camphora door → Magnoliaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Lauraceae is easiest to learn by contrast with magnolias: both are aromatic magnoliids, but laurels hide their reproductive architecture in tiny 3-part flowers and one-seeded fruits.

steps.title: 1 · Prove the leaf has no stipules
steps.look_for: Simple entire leaves attached without a stipular ring or persistent stipule scar.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Lauraceae from Magnoliaceae, where stipules leave conspicuous annular node scars.

steps.title: 2 · Find the 3+3 tepals
steps.look_for: Six small tepals arranged as two whorls of three around the stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: Three-part floral symmetry is a core Lauraceae pattern.

steps.title: 3 · Catch an anther opening by valves
steps.look_for: Tiny flap-like valves lifting upward from the anther instead of long slits opening down the side.
steps.why_it_matters: This is one of the strongest family characters in Lauraceae.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the flower to a one-seeded fruit
steps.look_for: A single fleshy fruit seated on an enlarged pedicel or shallow cupule.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the tiny flower to a visually useful fruit architecture.

steps.title: 5 · Lindera door
steps.look_for: Deciduous shrub; flowers appear before or with leaves in small pseudoumbels enclosed by paired bracts; plants mostly dioecious; mature fruit bright red.
steps.why_it_matters: A strong native Texas spicebush package within the family.

steps.title: 6 · Camphora door
steps.look_for: Evergreen tree with strongly aromatic foliage, leaves commonly with 3 strong basal/near-basal veins and small panicles of flowers; introduced in Texas.
steps.why_it_matters: Visually separates the introduced camphor-tree concept from deciduous spicebush.

comparisons.title: Lauraceae vs Magnoliaceae
comparisons.rule: Lauraceae lacks stipules, has tiny 3-merous flowers with valvate anthers, and usually a single-seeded drupe/berry. Magnoliaceae has stipules/node scars, very large flowers with numerous tepals/stamens/pistils, and an aggregate fruit of many follicles.

comparisons.title: Lauraceae vs Saururaceae
comparisons.rule: Lauraceae project plants are woody with tiny tepaled flowers and a one-seeded fruit; Saururaceae is a rhizomatous wetland herb with stipular sheaths, no perianth, and many tiny flowers packed into a raceme/spike.

comparisons.title: Lindera vs Camphora
comparisons.rule: Lindera benzoin is deciduous, mostly dioecious, and flowers in spring pseudoumbels before/with leaves; Camphora officinarum is evergreen, strongly camphor-scented, commonly triplinerved, and is introduced in Texas.

visual_lesson.caveat: Aroma is helpful but should not be the only crew test. Generic placement in Lauraceae often depends on flower/fruit details; use visible venation, inflorescence and reproductive characters whenever possible.

genera.fast_cue: deciduous aromatic shrub + pre-leaf pseudoumbels + mostly dioecious flowers + red drupe
evergreen aromatic tree + often 3-veined leaves + small flowers + black/purple one-seeded fruit
